<description>
This PR fixes #29220

- The PR adds a wallet `-maxfeerate` startup option, as the upper limit of wallet transactions fee rate.

- This fixes the ambiguity of using `maxtxfee` value to check the upper limit of transactions fee rate.

-  Wallet will not create a transaction with fee rate above `maxfeerate` value.

- This PR adds a functional test that ensure the behavior is enforced.

* If the user can set both `relayMinFee` and `maxtxfee`, I think we need to have a sanity check at startup to make sure they are not setting insane values that could result in them creating stuck transactions
* I think its okay to use a "fake transaction size" for a sanity check, but we should probably call it that i.e. `BASELINE_TX_SIZE = <1000, or maybe a minimum tx size?>`. That way, it is used consistently throughout the codebase, has a comment explaining what it used for and what it shouldn't be used for, etc
* There are a few other places where we use `maxtxfee` to calculate a fake feerate (such as `settxfee`). We should change those to use `maxtxfeerate`

In general, I agree we should always use `maxtxfeerate` when checking things about feerates. The only exception is during startup where we need to compare `maxtxfee` to other user set values relating to feerates.

It is deterministically reproducible on my NixOS Ryzen 7 7700 using:
```
build/test/functional/test_runner.py -j160 (seq 160 | xargs -I{} echo wallet_fundrawtransaction)
```
The issue is that in `createTransactionInternal`, I was using `nBytes` to calculate the fee rate.
This is incorrect because `nBytes` is the virtual size calculated using `CalculateMaximumSignedTx`. There are cases where `nBytes` is overestimated, and in that case, the fee rate will turn out to be much lower than it actually is, so the wallet will go ahead and allow creation of the tx.
But when we broadcast the tx, `BroadcastTransaction` uses the actual transaction vsize and fee to compute the fee rate  it will turn out to be slightly higher than `maxfeerate`, so the node will not broadcast to peers or add the tx to the mempool. The tx is then marked untrusted and will not be used in future transactions.
Because the next test depends on the untrusted tx being available, the test fails with insufficient funds.
I fixed this by using `GetVirtualTransactionSize` to compute the fee rate.
After that fix, the test failure is now obvious: we fail the `maxfeerate` check because it will be exceeded before proceeding to broadcast the transaction.
This can be tested by running f835281aec52bafec9e4255d183ff22057ac8918 without the test changes.
So I had to update the test to bump `maxfeerate` to allow creating a tx with a high fee rate.
`rpc_psbt.py` also relies on high fee rate txs, so I updated the nodes to account for that.

You can verify the issue no longer happens by running without failure

```
build/test/functional/test_runner.py -j160 (seq 160 | xargs -I{} echo wallet_fundrawtransaction)
```

After reviewing this PR again, I asked some clankers to take a look at the code to see if I missed something and they found a bug.

tldr: Using sendall can return `true` for a transaction that can't enter to the mempool as it can be silently paying more fees than the allowed by `-maxfeerate`.

Clankers full explanation:

```
sendall's creation-time -maxfeerate check ignores bump fees for
unconfirmed inputs, while the broadcast-time check in BroadcastTransaction
includes them.  When fee_rate is set exactly equal to -maxfeerate and the
wallet spends unconfirmed inputs with positive bump fees, the creation check
passes (equality, ignoring bump fees) but the broadcast check fails (actual
fee > max_rate.GetFee(actual_vsize)).  The error is silently swallowed by
CommitTransaction, so sendall returns {"complete": true, "txid": ...} for a
transaction that never entered the mempool.
```

I've asked the clankers to code a functional test that proves the incorrect behavior: https://github.com/polespinasa/bitcoin/commit/62fa2e2428028043c4462ba5b5431c3d139473d0
